newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico primary Cetes rates may ease more - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico primary Cetes rates may ease more - analysts.

text.p: Mexico's primary Cetes rates may ease again at Banco de Mexico's primary auction on Monday, as demand remains strong, analysts said.
Investors looking to lock in high real returns will help push down the treasury bill rates, one analyst told Reuters.
Analysts are looking for a decline of up to 50 basis points in the one-month paper at the auction, which will take place on Monday this week because of the May day holiday on Thursday.
At the auction last week, the bellwether 28-day rate fell 238 basis points to 20.23 percent.
Market watchers MMS International forecast that rates will remain broadly stable at this week's auction, with perhaps some easing. They added that many analysts are calling for lower rates.
Mexico's fundamentals favor lower interest rates, with forward real rates close to 10 percent at present, brokerage house Abaco said in a report on Monday.
The fall in the 28-day Cetes rate last week, was due to an increase in liquidity related to the build-up of reserves at the central bank, it said.
That liquidity is finding its way into the money base. In the first two weeks of April, net reserves rose by over $1.0 billion.
The central bank neutralized a lot of this by selling repurchase agreements for 20.77 billion pesos over this month, Abaco said.
"Nonetheless, liquidity is still somewhat high and may be even higher in the next few days as 30.0 billion pesos of central bank short-term loans are paid back," it said.
"Nonetheless, the fundamentals are also in favor of lower rates, as forward real rates at present are close to 10 percent," Abaco said.
Abaco said it continues to recommend 182-day Cetes.
